newsitem.title: USA: S. Carolina governor calls for $250 mln GO bonds.
newsitem.headline: S. Carolina governor calls for $250 mln GO bonds.

text.p: South Carolina Gov. David Beasley called for a $250 million comprehensive general obligation bond bill for schools and public safety as part of his proposed $4.6 billion budget for fiscal 1998.
The budget released Tuesday preserves the property tax cuts adopted last year, exempting homes valued at $100,000 or less.

Beasley proposed that at least 90 percent of the Property Tax Relief Fund used to offset those lost revenues should come from recurring sources, and that certain non-recurring surplus revenues also be earmarked to offset property tax cuts.
The governor also called for eliminating the contingent spending of unprojected surplus funds and closer scrutiny of capital projects included in bond bills.
All above items make up a package of safeguards that the governor considers non-negotiable.
"If any part of this package is compromised I will veto the entire effort," he said.

Beasley's budget projects revenue growth of 3.6 percent for fiscal 1998. It allocates $7.1 million for debt service payment, $3.3 million for general reserve fund contributions, $2.2 million for the capital reserve fund and $26.8 million for the local government fund.
It allocates $249 million, or 44 percent of new spending, for education. It would boost teacher pay by an average of more than $1,000 a year, and add $17 million to a full-day kindergarten program.
Beasley proposed allocating $400,000 to begin a prepaid tuition assistance program allowing parents to pay college tuition costs at today's prices.
The state's General Assembly convenes Jan 14. Beasley said he would address state highway needs within the next few weeks, which could result in an additional bond proposal.
The state pays about $157 million annually in debt service. Without new borrowing, that amount will drop steadily in the next few years as oustanding bonds are retired.
